title: Things You Should Never Do, Part I
summary: Joel Spolsky's 2000 essay: rewriting from scratch (Netscape, Borland) is the worst strategic mistake because old code embodies fixes, reading is harder than writing, and every class of problem can be fixed in place.

assertions.quote: When you throw away code and start from scratch, you are throwing away all that knowledge. All those collected bug fixes.
It's harder to read code than to write it.
These problems can be solved, one at a time, by carefully moving code, refactoring, changing interfaces.
there is absolutely no reason to believe that you are going to do a better job than you did the first time
